chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, all from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon the death of his master) who killed a man in error, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his master so desires, he can pay the wergild to them, or else hand him over to them, for him to serve them. So when his master dies, meaning the one who promised to free him, he would return as free. And in the report of Yunus: There would be nothing upon him.'

key_terms.مُدَبَّر: Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon the death of his master)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mudabbir who commits accidental homicide?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific legal status of a *Mudabbir* in cases of accidental homicide, highlighting the master's discretion between paying *diyah* or providing the slave as service (*kafalah*) to the victim's family. The alternative narration in Yunus's chain, stating 'no penalty,' reflects the scholarly discussion on whether the *Mudabbir*’s partial freedom exempts him from the full financial burden, a nuance often analyzed in Shia jurisprudence regarding the intersection of manumission and blood money. This hadith is foundational in *al-Kafi* for understanding how partial manumission affects liability in *diyah* cases.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Humran,

(It has been narrated) both together from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon the death of his master), who killed a man in error. Heasws said: ‘If his master so desires to he can pay the wergild to them, or else hand him over to them, for him to serve them. So when his master dies, meaning the one who (promised to) free him, he would return as free’. And in another report of Yunus: ‘There would be nothing upon him’.
